negative_findings.description: Every attempted direct fetch of bank.gov.ua (supervision/payment-services) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to the plain fetch tool.
negative_findings.result_summary: 403 on the regulator's own domain; PDFs under /admin_uploads/ and /files/ appeared in search indexes, so the site is presumed live and bot-defended rather than dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important source in this cell cannot be collected with a naive HTTP client; the pipeline needs a browser-based fetcher or the collection will silently under-report the primary regulator.

negative_findings.description: Could not pin the canonical URL for NBU Board Resolution No. 81 of 25.07.2025 (authorisation of non-financial payment service providers) or for the NBU draft-regulations consultation listing page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both are attested by secondary sources (law-firm briefings; NBU-hosted draft PDF at /admin_uploads/article/proekt_pr_2026-05-26.pdf) but the exact landing URLs were not observed in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Resolution 81 defines the TPP authorisation gate and the 31.12.2025 / 01.01.2027 deadlines; the consultations page is the cell's earliest-warning channel. Both must be resolved by hand before automated collection.

negative_findings.description: No machine-readable (API/CSV/open-data) endpoint for the Payment Infrastructure Register (Реєстр платіжної інфраструктури) was located in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: The register is described in NBU news and supervision pages, but only HTML/PDF presentation was evidenced; no data.gov.ua dataset was confirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Tracking who holds a payment-services licence over time is the backbone of vendor/acquirer market intelligence; without a structured feed this needs scraping plus snapshot diffing.

negative_findings.description: The NBU-approved open banking technical API specification itself was not found as a published document.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sources indicate the NBU has up to 18 months from Resolution 80 (25.07.2025) to approve the technical specification, and that legal-entity account specs were still being finalised by the Open API Group.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The specification is the artefact that actually binds vendors; its publication date is the key event to watch in this cell over the next collection cycles.

brief: Ukraine's payments rulebook is unusually concentrated: the NBU is both legislator-in-practice and supervisor, and nearly every binding artefact in this cell — the Law on Payment Services (No. 1591-IX), Resolution No. 80 (open banking, 25.07.2025), Resolution No. 81 (non-financial PSP authorisation), the SEP-4.1 ISO 20022 rulebooks, and the payment infrastructure registers — originates on bank.gov.ua. That concentration is also the main operational risk: bank.gov.ua returned 403 to every plain fetch in this run, so collection needs a browser-based fetcher, with zakon.rada.gov.ua and docs.dtkt.ua as authoritative-enough mirrors. The genuinely non-NBU intelligence sits one layer out: the EMA Association's Open API Group actually drafts the Berlin Group-based API specification, UAFIC and the banking associations signal industry readiness and pushback, and the Verkhovna Rada bill tracker gives lead time before secondary acts appear. Highest-value watch items for the next cycle are the NBU consultations page (comment deadlines), the still-unpublished open banking technical API specification, and register diffs showing which PSPs and technological operators have completed re-licensing.
